After negotiating to ensure that Adumar would be united after the conflict, Antilles agreed to take command of an alliance formed by the other nations of Adumar not allied with Cartann, Janson joined him in a [[Adumari Civil War|massive airstrike]] on Cartann. The pilots were still in local craft, which placed them at a competitive disadvantage against the Imperial pilots flying TIE Interceptors. Though the [[Adumari Union]] achieved the element of surprise, they were outnumbered and outgunned. However, a group of commandos and intelligence personnel located the New Republic X-wings and Red Flight quickly blasted open a tunnel access of the ''perator''{{'s}} palace before taking to the skies to challenge the Imperial pilots. Having shot down three of the four TIEs, Red Flight also accepted the surrender of numerous Cartann squadrons after their ''perator'' was captured.<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" />

Only days after Cartann was defeated and Adumar united and preparing to join the New Republic, Janson and Red Flight again took to their fighters, this time to [[Battle of Adumar|defend]] against an Imperial attack force ostensibly sent to aid Cartann. Janson fought in the battle, shooting several TIE Interceptors off of Antilles. The New Republic and Adumari force was victorious over the Empire, and, mission accomplished, the pilots returned to the New Republic.<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" />

Some time after their successful mission, Janson, Celchu, and Klivian were interviewed by Hallis Saper aboard the ''Errant Venture'' as part of a [[holodocumentary]] on Adumar she was composing. In particular, Janson described the Adumari fascination with the blastsword and other aspects of the culture, even wearing his favorite cloak from Adumar as a memento of the trip.<ref name="Adumar: Pilots Wanted" />

====The end of the Galactic Civil War====
{{Quote|I wouldn't get too overconfident if I was you.|Janson, discussing the state of the Empire|<ref name="Specter of the Past">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref>}}
Janson, still with Rogue Squadron as of [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], was present under [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis's]] command during the [[Caamas Document]] crisis, and was one of the first to learn of the Bothan role in the attack on [[Caamas/Legends|Caamas]] on [[Morishim]], as he knew a little Morish. A native speaker was telling the public about the Bothan involvement and Janson translated the man's speech for the others. Janson, Celchu, Antilles, and Lando Calrissian went to the place of the [[Old Recluse]]&mdash;said to be the source of the information&mdash;only to find a fully equipped Imperial communications center that had fallen into local hands. Before they could fully investigate it, they were summoned back to their craft to intercept an Imperial Star Destroyer chasing a corvette. Despite the Rogues' efforts, the Star Destroyer captured the corvette and fled, though Lando did manage to intercept part of a transmission from the ship. Unbeknownst to them, the corvette was carrying Colonel [[Meizh Vermel]], an aide of [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon's]] who was carrying a meeting request for Bel Iblis, though Janson figured it was a simple theft-and-defection on the part of the corvette.<ref name="Specter of the Past" />

Sometime after the [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|end]] of the Galactic Civil War, Janson, along with many other Rogue pilots, retired from active duty.<ref name="Dark Tide I: Onslaught">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught]]''</ref> Janson was invited to the [[Wedding of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade]] in [[20 ABY/Legends|20 ABY]] as one of the guests. Janson was late for the wedding, but when he arrived, Antilles met him and enlisted his and Klivian's help. Antilles had caught word that a [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]] hired by Imperials was intent on disrupting the wedding. When they attacked, Janson and several other former Rogue pilots, including Celchu, as well as Jedi [[Kam Solusar]] and Chewbacca, fought them off. Janson and Klivian were sent to stall a group heading for the annex buildings, but were unarmed and outnumbered. The swoop gang members threatened to beat them when smuggler chief [[Booster Terrik]] emerged from the annex and threatened the swoop gang with bodily harm if they woke the children he'd been babysitting. Awed by Terrik's reputation and his quick knock-out punch delivered to one of the gang members, the others withdrew.<ref name="Star Wars: Union">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref>

===The Yuuzhan Vong War===
{{Quote|Sithspawn, I was flirting with a nine-year-old.''"<br />"''Nineteen. And she has more kills than the three of us put together at the same age.|Wes Janson and Tycho Celchu referring to Jaina Solo|<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref>}}
Janson later went on to found the volunteer squadron of A-wings and E-wings called the [[Taanab Yellow Aces]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. This squadron arrived to help Wedge Antilles and his New Republic forces in the [[Battle of Borleias (Yuuzhan Vong War; Second)|defense]] of [[Borleias/Legends|Borleias]] in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]] following the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Battle of Coruscant]]. Flying in escort of the transport ''[[Reckless Abandon]]'', Janson and his fighters fended off groups of alien [[Yorik-et|coralskipper]] fighters as New Republic fighters from Borleias arrived to escort him and his group to the planet. After the coralskippers were defeated, Janson flirted with [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] without knowing her identity. Upon landing on the planet and being welcomed by Antilles, Janson was informed who "Twin Suns Leader" was, to his surprise and chagrin. Janson then told Antilles that he and his pilots were on permanent assignment to assist the defense of Borleias.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" />

Janson and the Aces acquitted themselves well in the New Republic military as an elite starfighter squadron along with [[Twin Suns Squadron|Twin Suns]], [[Vanguard Squadron (Hapes)|Vanguard]], [[Blackmoon Squadron|Blackmoon]] and Rogue Squadrons during the Yuuzhan Vong siege of the planet. The Yellow Aces fought with distinction at Borleias, helping protect the [[pipefighter]] decoys in order to distract the Yuuzhan Vong from a strategic retreat. As the Yuuzhan Vong began a final push, Janson's Yellow Aces and the other elite squadrons escorted the pipefighters up for one last deception, only to abandon their charges and jump to assist the [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'', which was encroaching on the Yuuzhan Vong command [[Koros-Strohna|worldship]]. With Janson and the rest of the New Republic's elite squadrons flying cover for the massive ship and fending off waves of coralskippers, ''Lusankya'' executed [[Operation Emperor's Spear]], ramming the giant warship into the worldship to destroy it. Following the destruction of the worldship and the recapture of Borleias, Janson and the rest of the New Republic forces withdrew.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" /> The defensive action at Borleias allowed the New Republic to reorganize itself after a series of defeats and a new government dubbed the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] was formed, unifying much of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to combat the Yuuzhan Vong.<ref name="The Unifying Force" />

At [[Selvaris]], some four years [[29 ABY/Legends|into]] the war, Janson and the Yellow Aces helped the Galactic Alliance liberate captured troops from the turncoat [[Peace Brigade]] and the Yuuzhan Vong. Janson's squadron was tasked with destroying the forward gunships of the prisoner convoy. The prisoner transports were quickly secured and Janson's squad shifted to an escort role, protecting the transports as Yuuzhan Vong reinforcements arrived in the form of advanced [[Slayer ship|stingcrawler]] fighters, which easily punched through the Galactic Alliance lines and inflicted heavy damage. The Aces suffered casualties from their assault, but managed to escape with most of the transports. Janson and the Aces went on to participate in the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar|Recapture of Coruscant]], with his squadron helping escort the initial wave of troop transports to touch down on the galactic capital. When one transport was attacked by [[grutchin]] creatures and went out of control, the Yellow Aces followed it down to the surface, using their lasers to pick off the grutchins, but were unsuccessful in saving it. The Galactic Alliance was ultimately successful in retaking the planet and forcing the capitulation of the Yuuzhan Vong, ending the war.<ref name="The Unifying Force" />

===Second Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Is it over?|Wes Janson checking in as Rakehell Twelve prior to the Battle at Centerpoint Station|<ref name="Fury" />}}
In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], war broke out again as numerous star systems seceded from the Galactic Alliance to form the [[Confederation]], resulting in the [[Second Galactic Civil War]]. During the war, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] fell to the dark side of the Force and seized power in the Galactic Alliance, resulting in a schism between the [[New Jedi Order]] and the Galactic Alliance. As the Jedi and their [[Hapes/Legends|Hapan]] allies formulated plans to neutralize Solo, now styling himself "[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Darth]] Caedus," Caedus responded by kidnapping the [[Allana Djo Solo|daughter]] of the [[Tenel Ka Djo|Queen]] of Hapes. To prevent her from being held hostage, Luke Skywalker devised a mission that would both free the young Hapan princess Allana as well as neutralize the [[Centerpoint Station]] weapon, which the Galactic Alliance sought to seize.<ref name="Fury" />

Janson was one of many veteran pilots recruited by Wedge Antilles to support Luke Skywalker's combined mission, meeting with Skywalker on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] and learning of the Jedi's intention to free Allana. Janson flew with the other pilots in [[Rakehell Squadron]] as Rakehell Twelve during the operation to [[Battle of Centerpoint Station (Second Galactic Civil War)|destroy]] [[Centerpoint Station]] and rescue Allana. Upon arrival in the Corellia system, the Rakehells first flew cover for the infiltration team that boarded Solo's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] by pretending to chase a shuttle containing the boarding party into its hangar bay.<ref name="Fury" />

The Rakehells then repeated their procedure on a second shuttle, faking a chase that led to the subsequent insertion of a second Jedi-led team onto Centerpoint Station. Galactic Alliance fighters rose to challenge the Rakehells at that point, leading to the Janson battling against his former unit of Rogue Squadron. Both squadrons inflicted casualties on each other, but as a Confederation assault force arrived to contest Centerpoint Station, the Rogues were called to respond, leaving the Rakehells unengaged. Once Allana was rescued, the Rakehells then flew cover for the ''Millennium Falcon'' extracting the boarding party from Solo's ship by distracting hostile gunners with their strafing runs. Furthermore, the other sabotage party was successful in destroying Centerpoint Station, resulting in a total success for the Jedi faction in the battle. The Rakehells and their accompanying transports then withdrew to a space station orbiting [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]]. Janson survived the battle<ref name="Fury" /> and the Jedi ultimately [[Battle of Uroro Station|slew]] Caedus not long afterward to end the war.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Janson.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Janson in his flight suit.]]
{{Quote|I thought you'd be able to do what I never could: get Janson up to an emotional age of fourteen, maybe fifteen.''"<br />"''Nothing in the galaxy could do that. Not Darth Vader and the dark side of the Force, not the nuclear devastation of an exploding sun.|Wedge Antilles and Tycho Celchu|<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" />}}
Janson had dark [[Color/Legends|brown]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]], brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and stood at a height of 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="A Cast of Thousands" /> He was regarded as a joker, despite being a lethal opponent, being particularly accurate with blaster pistols and starfighter-grade weaponry.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" /> According to Skywalker, Janson was only truly happy when he was manning the guns of a Y-wing or an airspeeder. He was known for having a short temper, often having to be pulled out of cantina fights.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron" /> Janson was described as observant, using what he noticed as fodder for his witty remarks, mockery, or jokes.<ref name="Fury" /> He was generally cheerful and light-hearted, even in the face of opposition or boredom.<ref name="Fury" /><ref name="X-Wing: Iron Fist" />

Janson also considered himself a ladies' man, frequently seeking the attention of women he considered attractive.<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" /><ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: Mandatory Retirement" /> His flirtatious nature was amplified by a dark side temple on Malrev IV, leading to his solicitation of a female Bothan.<ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue" /> Janson's casual flirtations also led to him accidentally trying to attract the attention of Jaina Solo&mdash;he was shocked when he learned of her identity and regretted his pursuit.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" />

He enjoyed playing pranks on his fellow squad mates. He believed in having fun today, because tomorrow might not come. During his time in Wraith Squadron, he developed the character Lieutenant [[Kettch]], a fictional Ewok starfighter pilot.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" /> Kettch became a recurring theme in Janson's pranks.<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" /> This originated when he claimed that a candidate for Wraith Squadron was an Ewok,<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" /> and then it circulated among the Wraiths, including the time Wraith [[Slicer/Legends|slicer]] [[Castin Donn]] reprogrammed Antilles' TIE Interceptor to make his voice sound like an Ewok. This led to Antilles being forced to fly into battle, against Imperial forces, while wearing a stuffed Ewok in his lap.<ref name="X-Wing: Iron Fist" /> When the stuffed Ewok doll started showing up everywhere and appeared to move on its own, Antilles attached a transponder to it, leading to the discovery that Janson was placing the doll in those places. The Wraiths got back at Janson by convincing him that the real Kettch had gotten loose and he had to strip naked and cover himself in Ewok food to find and recapture it. The joke only ended when Lara Notsil found a real Ewok that fit Kettch's description exactly. She found this hilarious.<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" />

Due to his mischievous nature, Janson was not considered suitable to leave behind on the ground on Adumar to conduct sensitive diplomatic negotiations by Antilles. However, Janson was loyal to his friends and fellow pilots despite any good-natured grumbling or teasing he gave them when they needed his help. Janson was willing to keep watch all night long for Antilles during a covert rendezvous between Antilles and Iella Wessiri, and also placed his life at risk in order to save both Antilles and Cheriss ke Hanadi from possibly fatal injuries by engaging in a blastsword duel against an experienced duelist.<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" />

Janson did have a serious side though, that exhibited itself through grim, angry determination. It didn't come out often, but Janson apparently was in this mood when fighting or flying against an enemy of his.<ref name="X-wing: Starfighters of Adumar" /><ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" /> Janson also abandoned his typical jesting nature when discussing the incident where he was forced to kill fellow Rebel pilot Kissek Doran. Janson likewise displayed his serious side in a series of interactions with Doran's son, Kell Tainer, which ultimately led to the resolution of the conflict between them.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" />

During his career as a pilot and soldier, Janson was noted for his bravery, particularly during commando missions. Kell Tainer noted that Janson could probably make a fort out of all his bravery commendations. During ground combat, Janson was calm and controlled under fire, using his blaster skills to good effect<ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" /> or placing charges to destroy key facilities.<ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: In the Empire's Service" />

Post-retirement, Janson developed a sense of responsibility and initiative when he found, trained, and commanded the volunteer fighter squadron Taanab Yellow Aces. Janson remained with the squadron for over two years of the Yuuzhan Vong War, ruefully citing his responsibility to them as reason enough to remain with the squadron instead of transferring back into Rogue Squadron. His light-hearted and playful side remained, but Janson was still a skilled-enough pilot and trainer that his squadron was considered an elite unit alongside Rogue and Twin Suns Squadrons.<ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" />

==Behind the scenes==
Though Janson only had a few moments of screen time in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], his character received considerable attention in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], as he was featured extensively in the ''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]'' comics, novels in the [[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|''X-wing'' series]], as well as several later EU novels. In his ''Rogue Squadron'' comics, Janson's cheerful and jesting nature was established by writer [[Michael A. Stackpole|Michael Stackpole]],<ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: The Phantom Affair" /> as were his blaster pistol and gunnery skills.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron" />

Janson's novel appearances have mainly occurred in works written by [[Aaron Allston]]: ''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]'', ''[[X-Wing: Iron Fist]]'', ''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]'', ''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]'', ''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]'', and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]''. In the latter two novels, Allston brought Janson's character into the [[New Jedi Order era|New Jedi Order]] and [[Legacy era]]s with small cameos,<ref name="Fury" /><ref name="Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand" /> while he played a larger role in the three Wraith Squadron books.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron" /><ref name="X-Wing: Iron Fist" /><ref name="X-Wing: Solo Command" /> Janson has also been featured as a minor character in novels by other authors including [[Timothy Zahn]],<ref name="Specter of the Past" /> [[Matthew Stover]],<ref name="Mindor" /> and Michael Stackpole,<ref name="X-Wing: Isard's Revenge" /> as well as the ''[[Star Wars: Union]]'' comic.<ref name="Star Wars: Union" />

===Portrayal===
{{Quote|I play a stormtrooper, in a walker, who's trying to shoot down my own bloody plane.|Ian Liston, the actor who portrays Janson, on ''The Empire Strikes Back''|<ref name="Insider 32">{{InsiderCite|32|Rebel Pilot Reunion}}</ref>}}
Wes Janson was portrayed by [[Ian Liston]] in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. During filming of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', a call was put out for an actor, not an extra, to play an AT-AT gunner. That was Liston's original role in the film, but he was later asked by an assistant director with whom Liston had previously worked to take the role of Janson since the original actor had fallen ill. Thus he ironically played both an Imperial and a Rebel, and in one sequence of the film is in effect trying to shoot himself down.<ref name="Insider 32" /> Regarding his scenes as Janson with Wedge Antilles, Liston revealed in 2005 that the two actors were never actually on set together&mdash;Liston's double took his place when the scene focused on [[Denis Lawson]] (Antilles) and vice versa.<ref name="Insider 119">{{InsiderCite|119|In Their Own Words: Making The Empire Strikes Back|In Their Own Words: Making ''The Empire Strikes Back''}}</ref> In [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']], Janson is voiced by [[Terence McGovern]].

===Continuity errors===
[[File:Wes_Janson_Dead.jpg|thumb|left|Janson's death in Antilles' story]]
Janson's non-canon death was written in [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] [[Star Wars (1977) 78|''Star Wars'' (1977) 78]].<ref name="Star Wars 78: Hoth Stuff" /> The story was later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] to be a tall tale that Wedge would tell new recruits, only to startle them with Janson's appearance.<ref name="Hoth: Under the Ice" />''

Janson's helmet, like most, is modeled from [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], where it is worn by [[Puck Naeco/Legends|Puck Naeco]]. However, due to an editing gaffe, Naeco and his helmet can only be seen when [[Theron Nett/Legends|Theron Nett]] gets shot down later, [http://www.myuselessknowledge.com/swfa/ejecteject.gif as seen here].<ref name="Star Wars Customizable Card Game">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Theron Nett}}</ref>

In [[West End Games]]' first edition of ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', in Wedge's entry, his gunner is named "Derit Janson." Any other mention of Janson in the book uses the name "Wes." The error was corrected in the second edition.<ref name="GG3" /> In ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue]]'', Janson's homeworld is incorrectly listed as "Taanad."<ref name="X-wing Rogue Squadron: Requiem for a Rogue" /> In ''X-Wing: Wraith Squadron'' during the Battle of Ession, Janson was mistakenly listed as flying an X-wing during part of the battle. Author [[Aaron Allston]] has stated that this was a mistake and Janson is in a TIE fighter throughout the battle.<ref name="FAQ">{{WebCite|url=http://www.aaronallston.com/factpages/faq_starwars.html|text=Frequently Asked Questions: ''Star Wars'' Novels|work=[[Aaron Allston]]'s [https://web.archive.org/web/20150201124617/http://www.aaronallston.com official website]|archivedate=20150102092638|nolive=1}}</ref>

===Author and actor comments===
Aaron Allston, whose works have often featured Wes Janson, has stated that Janson is one of his favorite characters to write out of the characters which he did not invent.<ref name="FAQ" /> Janson has appeared or been mentioned in eight of Allston's novels. Ian Liston has followed the books and other appearances of Janson and called them "great fun." Liston has met Allston more than once and approves of the direction taken with Janson's character as a practical joker.<ref name="Insider 119" />
